description: Cross-binding conformance for the four model constructs no evaluator in the executing bindings runs: a CONTINUOUS EVENT (`continuous_events`), a DISCRETE EVENT (`discrete_events`), an IMPLICIT EQUATION (an equation whose LHS is an expression rather than a bare unknown, an indexed unknown, `D(unknown)` or `ic(unknown)`) and WIENER NOISE (a parameter whose `update.kind` is `wiener`, which makes the document an SDE; issue #475). Before issues #264 and #356 they validated and were then silently dropped by most evaluators: the event never fired and the residual was never solved, so a run reported a number the document does not describe. The decision this category pins is REFUSAL: an evaluator that cannot run the construct MUST fail the build with the diagnostic `unsupported_construct` (esm-spec §9.6.6), and the message MUST name the construct and the evaluator. It pins no numbers. The `control` case is the discrete-event array document with its event removed; it takes the same array evaluator and MUST still run, which is what attributes the refusals to the construct. Four cases put an event of each kind on an inline SUBSYSTEM, which Python's and Rust's flatten do not lift into the flattened system, and one spells an implicit equation as the time derivative of an expression (`D(a + b) ~ 3`). Two put an event of each kind on a REACTION SYSTEM, whose `continuous_events` / `discrete_events` blocks the schema grants on the same footing as a model's and which Julia's and Rust's flatten used to drop, so the refusal never fired and the document ran without its event. The coupled case puts the array continuous-event model next to a second model, which some bindings build through a different route. Julia's ModelingToolkit export runs both kinds of event and hands implicit equations to `mtkcompile`, so it is outside this category (it has no SDE lowering, and refuses the two Wiener-noise cases by name with `compiler_refused_rule`); Go and TypeScript do not simulate and only register the code.
